reason: The ceramic blocks appear to be the available material for making the porous root medium, but how to prepare them is not yet clear.
expectation: The inspection should reveal how the blocks can be processed into root medium.

effect: The wash bench turned the blocks into clean, checked porous growing medium, ready for the beds.
reaction: The crushing and leach check make the preparation feel physically purposeful.
reason: The clean medium belongs in the empty growing beds.
expectation: The medium will fill the beds while leaving air spaces for roots.

effect: The beds now contain porous medium, and the remaining goal is to water their shared loop.
reaction: The distinction between air spaces and dry medium is clear.
reason: The drinking water supply can fill the dry beds through their connected irrigation system.
expectation: Water will enter the shared loop and wet the growing medium.

effect: The shared loop now irrigates the beds, although the lettuce shelf still needs a wick; the chapter's goals are complete.
reaction: The distinction between the wet beds and the still-unwicked lettuce shelf was a useful detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Preparing the ceramic medium was most worthwhile: breaking, washing and leach-checking it explained how local material could support roots without trapping water.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the beds was straightforward and predictable, though it made clear that porous medium alone was not enough.

surprise.text: I expected watering to wet all three beds, so the lettuce shelf still needing a wick changed my understanding of the shared circuit.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the preparation, filling and watering each had a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the lettuce shelf is wicked and the crops are established; the practical details made that next stage interesting.
